rationale: A well-motivated consolidation of two independently validated legs (GP/EV value metric and the dual unrecorded-capital floors), though the reviewer should note that gross profit now enters both legs (GP/EV numerator and the gross-margin floor), so part of any gain may be mechanical overlap rather than two independent channels.

The stated justification is internally wrong — nesting SUMRANKs re-ranks the inner composite, so the four channels do not carry exact quarter weights — and beyond that this is a kitchen-sink aggregation of already-tested legs whose outcome will be hard to attribute to any specific economic mechanism.

A clean single-lever diagnostic on the archive's strongest signal that directly tests whether the newly found margin-moat channel is firm-specific mispricing or an industry cost-structure tilt, with a defensible prior for why the answer may differ from the R&D-floor case.

The stated mechanism is inconsistent — EBITDA is already pre-amortisation, so "pre-amortisation gross profit" gives no reason to prefer GP over the incumbent numerator — leaving this a largely cosmetic numerator swap on an already-tested rank-difference signal.

The tie-mass diagnosis for the earlier conjunction failure is credible, but the test is confounded because both the value and moat legs are built from gross profit and no SUMRANK(GP/EV, margin floor) baseline exists in the archive, so a conjunction-versus-average inference will not be clean.

Distance of current gross margin from its own five-year peak is a genuinely untested state variable in this archive that plausibly separates depreciating from intact unrecorded capital, though the bounded-at-zero mass point means the long leg is effectively selected on the value leg alone and the signal may partly proxy margin momentum rather than intangible durability.
